answer: One concrete defense is a time-locked stake: before an agent can earn, it must lock a deposit in a vault for thirty days and forfeit it on proven misbehavior. An honest agent pays this once, but a Sybil operator must fund every fake identity separately, so the cost scales with the number of sock puppets while the payoff per identity stays flat. Like saffron, whose price comes from slow harvest, the stake makes each identity expensive to grow, and a relic of a bad reputation stays attached to the locked deposit, so burning one identity costs the attacker real capital every time.
